title: Lutnick follow-ups: Nvidia chip curbs, Tether and Iran, crypto council
summary: Each of the five leads matches real, dated reporting or official documents. Axios (11 Nov 2026) reported, from unnamed sources, that Lutnick held up Trump-approved curbs on firms suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China. Blumenthal's PSI minority staff tied Tether's USDT to Iranian shadow banking (28 Sep 2026) and then pressed Cantor (8 Oct 2026) on any Tether loan behind the Lutnick ownership transfer. By executive order, the Commerce Secretary sits on the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets. Cantor's $2B bitcoin-lending business exists, but Tether's part in it was only ever reported as talks. On tariff refunds, Cantor salespeople pitched refund-rights trades. Cantor says it never executed one, and no profit is documented. Every policy-for-family-gain link is still an allegation, and Commerce and Cantor deny them.

sub_claims.statement: Axios (Nov 2026) reports Lutnick stalled curbs on Nvidia-chip diversion to China.
sub_claims.finding: Confirmed as reporting, not as established fact. Axios scoops on 11 Nov 2026, citing unnamed high-level sources, say Trump approved action against suspected diverters at least three times in 2026. They say Lutnick held it up, warning it 'will start a trade war with China', and that Bessent confronted him in the Situation Room over Megaspeed, a Singapore firm. Commerce spokesperson Kristen Eichamer called the Bessent exchange false and did not address the rest. Coverage adds that BIS has made no Entity List additions since Oct 2025, that the Megaspeed probe was paused at DOJ's request, and that NYT reported an under secretary halted it after Nvidia intervened. Megaspeed says inspections found no illegal transfers. Reuters relayed the Axios report, but no independent confirmation of the internal deliberations was found.

sub_claims.statement: Sen. Blumenthal is probing Tether's alleged role in Iranian shadow banking.
sub_claims.finding: Blumenthal is ranking member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. On 28 Sep 2026 his minority staff released 'Tethered to Terrorism'. It found that 84% of 846 assessed sanctioned or seizure-targeted Iran-linked crypto wallets transacted mainly in USDT. Letters went to Treasury Secretary Bessent and to the Attorney General the same day, referring the findings. This is a minority-staff report, not a committee finding or an enforcement action. Tether says it helped freeze about $550M of Iran-linked USDT in 2026. Ardoino later claimed a 94% drop in Iran-linked volumes but gave no stated methodology. Audit note: coverage of the report breaks the 846 wallets down by designating authority. About 87% of the 757 Israel-designated wallets transacted mainly in USDT, against 57% of the 101 OFAC-designated wallets, so the headline 84% is driven mostly by Israeli designations.

sub_claims.statement: Blumenthal is also probing the Tether loan to the Lutnick children's trust.
sub_claims.finding: The 8 Oct 2026 letter went to Cantor chairman Brandon Lutnick, not to the Commerce Secretary. It makes 13 requests with a 23 Oct deadline. Coverage says these include the terms of Howard Lutnick's exit, any Tether loan or financial support that helped move the stake to his children, and the custody and reserve arrangements. It also cites more than $250M paid to Howard Lutnick, including a $192M Cantor distribution, and Blumenthal's ~$10B estimate for Cantor's Tether position. Summaries describe the loan as financing for 'his children'. The 'Dynasty Trust A' framing comes from Bloomberg (18 Mar 2026) and the Warren/Wyden letters (29 Apr 2026), covered in C35. No public reply from Cantor was found.

sub_claims.statement: Lutnick (possibly) sits on the White House crypto council.
sub_claims.finding: EO 14178 (23 Jan 2025) set up the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets, chaired by AI & crypto czar David Sacks. It names the Secretary of Commerce as a member. Lutnick is listed in 2025 coverage of the group's 30 Jul 2025 report, along with Bessent and Atkins. Trump also tasked Lutnick and Bessent with budget-neutral ways to acquire bitcoin. Sludge, Salon and Accountable.US flagged the Tether conflict in Feb 2025 and urged recusal. Lutnick declined to commit to recusing at confirmation, and no recusal from the working group was found. His actual involvement in the group's work is not documented.

sub_claims.statement: Cantor runs a ~$2B bitcoin-lending programme with Tether.
sub_claims.finding: Cantor announced a $2B bitcoin-backed financing business in July 2024, with more $2B tranches planned. In Nov 2024 Bloomberg reported Cantor was in talks for Tether to back it, as one of several funders. Launch coverage in 2025 names FalconX (~$100M first loan) and Maple Finance as borrowers, and Anchorage Digital and Copper as custodians. None of the launch reports found confirms that Tether ended up funding the programme. 'With Tether' is unverified beyond the talks stage.

sub_claims.statement: Lutnick's sons run Cantor deals that depend on Commerce/tariff policy, e.g. trading tariff-refund claims.
sub_claims.finding: In July 2025 Wired reported that Cantor salespeople offered to buy importers' IEEPA tariff-refund rights at 20-30% of duties paid. One email claimed a ~$10M trade had 'already' been done. After the Supreme Court's February 2026 tariff ruling, Rep. Raskin (House Judiciary ranking member) wrote to Howard and Brandon Lutnick on 27 Feb 2026 asking for records and raised insider-information concerns. Cantor says it 'has never executed any transactions or taken any position on tariffs refund claims': salespeople explored the idea and the firm dropped it. Semafor reported Cantor did not profit from the ruling. The pitch is documented. A completed trade or any profit is not. Tariffs are set by the President, USTR and Commerce, so the conflict concern is plausible but unproven. Audit note: Sens. Wyden and Warren had already written to Brandon Lutnick on 14 Aug 2025 asking how many refund agreements Cantor drafted or sold. Raskin's letter cites internal documents claiming about $10M in trades. Those documents have not been published, so Cantor's 'never executed' denial is contested but not disproved.

corrections: The claim implies Blumenthal's loan probe targets the Commerce Secretary. The 8 Oct 2026 letter was addressed to Cantor chairman Brandon Lutnick. Warren and Wyden wrote to Howard Lutnick and Tether directly on 29 Apr 2026.
'Crypto council' is the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets (EO 14178). Commerce's seat is set by the order, not 'possible'.
Tether's role in Cantor's $2B bitcoin-lending business is documented only as talks (Bloomberg, Nov 2024), not as a confirmed funder.
No tariff-refund trade by Cantor is documented. Wired reported a sales pitch and an email claiming a ~$10M trade, and Cantor says none was executed.
denials_and_context: Commerce (spokesperson Kristen Eichamer) called Axios's account of a Bessent-Lutnick Situation Room confrontation false, and did not immediately address the claim that Lutnick stalled the curbs. The Axios reporting rests on unnamed sources.
Megaspeed says Nvidia, Malaysia's trade ministry and BIS inspections found no illegal chip transfers. The Megaspeed probe was reportedly paused at DOJ's request.
Tether: USDT 'is not a haven for sanctioned actors'. It says it helped freeze ~$550M of Iran-linked USDT in 2026 and claims a 94% volume drop, with no stated methodology.
Cantor: it never executed or held tariff-refund positions. Commerce: Lutnick 'has no insight or strategic control over Cantor Fitzgerald'.
Cantor previously declined to give the size or use of the Tether loan. It says the trusts' purchase was funded from multiple sources at market terms (see C35).
The congressional probes are led by Democrats in the minority without subpoena power (Blumenthal at PSI, Warren and Wyden, Raskin). None alleges a specific crime by Lutnick.

Research limits: blumenthal.senate.gov could not be read directly, and other direct fetches were not attempted for most news sites. Findings rest on search summaries that agree across several outlets. Cantor's replies to the Raskin and Blumenthal letters, and any result of those inquiries, were not found.

Commerce (spokesperson Kristen Eichamer) denies the Bessent-Lutnick Situation Room confrontation. Secondary coverage relays Financial Times reporting that Commerce is holding up the Megaspeed blacklisting. Megaspeed denies moving chips illegally, and Nvidia says it put Megaspeed on its own block list in June 2025.

changes: Fresh searches (Axios/Reuters relays, The Block, HSGAC PDFs, Decrypt, Bloomberg relays, NOTUS) confirm all five core findings. Nothing was contradicted, and verdict and confidence are unchanged.
Added a wallet breakdown to the Tether-Iran sub-claim: 87% of 757 Israel-designated wallets and 57% of 101 OFAC-designated wallets. This nuance cuts in Tether's favour.
Tariff sub-claim: added the earlier Wyden-Warren letter of 14 Aug 2025, and noted that Raskin cites unpublished internal documents claiming about $10M in trades, so the denial is contested.
Cantor lending: still no source confirms Tether funding. The first loans (FalconX, Maple) are dated May 2025. The 'talks only' framing is kept.
Added to denials: Commerce's denial of the Bessent clash, the FT report (via secondary coverage) of the Megaspeed hold-up, and the Megaspeed and Nvidia statements.
